html:
SMTO-SKL-0001 — SMTO is missing a part it needs to work with databases

GUID: 23c1956e-0e8e-4b0f-b6e9-b5aefc1dd698
Slug: dependency-unavailable
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: skl

What happened

  • SMTO's database tools need a piece of supporting software that isn't installed on the computer running SMTO. No database query was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who installed SMTO to run the installer again (./install.sh) on the computer that runs SMTO. The installer adds the missing database software; allowing the Database Skill in Settings does not install it.
  2. When the installer has finished and no Tasks are running, restart SMTO. A restart makes SMTO load the newly installed database software.
  3. Ask your database question again in a new message. Nothing was run the first time, so asking again is safe once the software is installed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO answers your database request instead of showing this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who installed SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder, Gateway pairing or saved settings to fix this; the installer repairs the software in place.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Database Skill is unavailable because the Server's Python environment cannot import its declared sqlglot SQL-parsing dependency, so the check stops before any query runs.

What this means

  • Dependency availability checks report a missing required runtime library, including SQL parsing support, before the affected capability can operate. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Dependency availability checks report a missing required runtime library, including SQL parsing support, before the affected capability can operate.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the missing dependency and owning Controller or Gateway from the concrete producer.

How to fix it

  • On the Server host, rerun ./install.sh from the matching checkout (sqlglot>=26,<27 is declared in pyproject.toml) and confirm python -c "import sqlglot" succeeds in the Server's environment, then restart the Server once active work has finished. Repair in place without deleting Gateway pairing, credentials or settings; granting the Skill permission does not install dependencies.
  • The smTO runtime is missing a required library or has an incompatible dependency. Rerun ./install.sh on the server from the matching checkout and restart it after installation succeeds. If the diagnostic identifies a Gateway-side client instead, repair that selected Gateway with its platform installer, then refresh metadata.
  • From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • Restart the repaired server after installation succeeds and active work is settled. If a Gateway environment was repaired, restart that Gateway, refresh its metadata and start a new task. Reconcile any uncertain operations before repeating them.
  • Confirm the named dependency loads in the failing server or Gateway environment and its installer audit passes before retrying.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the named dependency loads in the failing server or Gateway environment and its installer audit passes before retrying. Reconcile any uncertain operations before repeating them.

How to verify the fix

  • The matching supported installation provides the dependency and the capability's availability check passes.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
